record.paper_title: Open Problems within Nonextensive Statistical Mechanics
record.original_question: Can a generalized product for NSM be defined from the properties of multivariate heavy-tailed q-statistical distributions, so that it plays for those distributions the role that ordinary multiplication plays in forming multivariate distributions of independent variables? The desired definition should avoid relying on the existing q-product when that form does not produce the structure of multivariate heavy-tailed distributions.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4: While the q-product is often referenced regarding its role in defining q-independence, the form does not lead to the structure of the multivariate heavy-tailed distributions in the manner that the product of distributions equates with the multivariate distribution of independent variables. A definition for the generalized product for NSM is needed that is based on the properties of the multivariate distributions, as was proposed in [43].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In nonextensive statistical mechanics one works with the q-deformed calculus: for q ∈ ℝ, the q-exponential is exp_q(x) = [1+(1−q)x]_+^{1/(1−q)} (with exp_1 = exp), and the q-product of two positive numbers x, y is x ⊗_q y = [x^{1−q} + y^{1−q} − 1]_+^{1/(1−q)}. Univariate q-Gaussians (q-statistical heavy-tailed distributions, 1 < q < 3) are densities of the form f_q(x) ∝ exp_q(−β x^2). A natural multivariate generalization is the family of multivariate heavy-tailed q-Gaussians on ℝ^d, f_q^{(d)}(x) ∝ exp_{q_d}(−x^⊤ Σ^{-1} x), with a dimension-dependent index q_d.

In ordinary probability theory, joint distributions of independent random variables factor as products of their marginals. The q-product was introduced to play an analogous role with respect to q-independence at the level of q-exponentials, but applying ⊗_q to the marginals of a multivariate heavy-tailed q-Gaussian does not reproduce the joint multivariate q-Gaussian density.

Problem. Construct a binary (or, more generally, d-ary) operation ⊙ acting on suitable classes of nonnegative functions (or on q-exponential / q-Gaussian densities), and a rule for transforming the deformation indices, with the following properties:

(i) For each d ≥ 2 and each admissible q, the operation reconstructs the multivariate heavy-tailed q-Gaussian density on ℝ^d from its univariate q-Gaussian marginals, in the same way that ordinary multiplication reconstructs the joint density of independent variables from their marginals.

(ii) In the limit q → 1, the operation reduces to ordinary pointwise multiplication of densities.

(iii) The construction is derived from intrinsic properties of multivariate heavy-tailed q-statistical distributions, rather than from the algebraic form of the existing q-product (which is to be used only where it is consistent with the multivariate heavy-tailed structure).

Provide such an operation, or prove that no operation satisfying (i)–(iii) exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A "coupled-product" for multivariate coupled-exponentials, addressing the construction of multivariate q-Gaussians from univariate ones with a dimension-dependent coupling κ_d = κ/(1+dκ), was proposed by Nelson (Physica A, 2015). This is the construction referenced as the starting point for the open problem, but the problem as posed asks for a more complete generalized product based intrinsically on properties of multivariate heavy-tailed q-distributions, and is still listed as an open problem in 2024.

status_evidence.title: A definition of the coupled-product for multivariate coupled-exponentials
status_evidence.snippet: The coupled-product and coupled-exponential of the generalized calculus of nonextensive statistical mechanics are defined for multivariate functions ... κ_d = κ/(1+dκ) ... enables construction of the multivariate coupled-Gaussian from univariate coupled-Gaussians.
status_evidence.claim: A multivariate coupled-product has been proposed that constructs multivariate q-Gaussians from univariate ones, partially addressing the problem.

status_evidence.title: On multivariate generalizations of the q-central limit theorem consistent with nonextensive statistical mechanics
status_evidence.snippet: Multivariate generalizations of the q-central limit theorem within nonextensive statistical mechanics.
status_evidence.claim: Multivariate q-statistical structures are an active topic but a fully satisfactory generalized product remains under discussion.
